options.label: Hyur
options.description: Modest of build and stature, the Hyur can lay claim to being the single most populous race in all of modern Eorzea, where they make up a prominent share of the populace in each of the realm's great city-states.

options.label: Elezen
options.description: Slender of body and long of limb, the Elezen were once the predominant race of all Eorzea, and to this day harbor a deep pride at being the chosen race of the gods. They boast a longer lifespan than most races by a slight margin.

options.label: Lalafell
options.description: Stocky and squat of stature, the Lalafell are by far the most diminutive of Eorzea's races. Typically maintaining a youthful appearance even in advancing years, a Lalafell's true age is ofttimes difficult for members of other races to ascertain.

options.label: Miqo'te
options.description: A race distinguished by their large, feline ears and supple tail. For reasons that are not entirely clear, female Miqo'te vastly outnumber males, a phenomenon rare among Eorzea's races.

options.label: Roegadyn
options.description: Massive and heavily muscled, the Roegadyn are easily the most imposing of Eorzea's races. Oft seen vying with one another in feats of strength, they can appear barbaric to the uneducated observer, but in fact are known to be an honorable and compassionate people. The histories are filled with tales of Roegadyn warriors and their courageous deeds.

options.label: Au Ra
options.description: Hailing from the Far Eastern continent of Othard, the Au Ra were a rare sight in Eorzea until most recently, when increasing unrest in their homeland forced a not-insignificant number of their people to journey west in search of asylum.

options.label: Viera
options.description: Of tall stature and slender frame, the Viera's physical appearance is strikingly similar to that of the Hyur and Elezen, save for their distinctive long ears. Adhering to a strict code known as the Green Word, they are prohibited from contact with the outside world under threat of exile. Their society is purely matriarchal, and males of age are seldom, if ever, found within the bounds of any village. They instead serve as protectors of the wood from the shadows, that no evil may ever encroach on their sacred lands.

options.label: Hrothgar
options.description: Hailing from the distant shores of Ilsabard, the Hrothgar are a burly people of lionlike appearance—or the males are, at least. Females number staggeringly few among their population, and thus are rarely so much as glimpsed by the other races.

options.label: Midlanders
options.description: The most populous clan of the most populous race, comprising over half of all Hyur, Midlanders can be found in city-states and villages the realm over, earning their keep in myriad trades and vocations. A highly cultured people, Midlanders have traditionally compensated for their lack of exceptional physical prowess with enterprise and ingenuity, contributing to great advances in all manner of disciplines. Indeed, many of the realm's greatest inventors and innovators have been Midlanders. With some exceptions, a comparatively large number of Midlanders are educated in letters from a young age, giving rise to a healthy population of academics and intellectuals.

options.label: Highlanders
options.description: Descendants of a people who followed the stars to the mountains of Gyr Abania in the wake of the Sixth Umbral Calamity, the Highlanders founded the city-state of Ala Mhigo, a bastion of military might until its fall to the Garlean invasion two decades agone. Many stayed behind, and now live a toilsome life under the yoke of their imperial masters, while those that fled their homeland now live as refugees in Eorzea. Their numbers are great in the Shroud but greater in Thanalan, where their presence has resulted in no small degree of social strife. Among the refugees are those who have put their considerable martial talents to use as sellswords and gladiators.

options.label: Wildwood Elezen
options.description: The ancestors of the Wildwood Elezen were displaced from their ancestral home on the plains when the Hyur came, migrating in part to Coerthas, where they established the nation of Ishgard, and in part to the Shroud, where they formed the nation of Gelmorra (the ancient subterranean state that predates Gridania). Though nowadays "Wildwood" is typically used to refer to the forest-dwelling Elezen, the Elezen of Ishgard, too, share the same common ancestry. As such, Gridania and Ishgard have traditionally enjoyed close relations, with each nation readily coming to the other's aid in times of need.

options.label: Duskwight Elezen
options.description: Making their home in deep forest caves and caverns for centuries, the Duskwight Elezen are the descendants of those who parted ways with their brethren after the founding of Gelmorra, choosing instead to remain in the stone-hewn chambers of Gelmorra or seek out new subterranean sanctums. Shunning the fetters of government and society, a great majority of the Duskwight keep a wide berth of the city-states, with some even resorting to brigandry as a means of survival. As a result, they are often looked upon with scorn by the citizens of Gridania, and those who have chosen to make their home in the city often suffer undue discrimination at the hands of their neighbors.

options.label: Plainsfolk
options.description: Seen in the greatest numbers on Vylbrand, the Plainsfolk trace their history to the maritime traders who settled in Limsa Lominsa to deal in pillaged and plundered wares. In the years to follow, they were joined by their families, who would become pioneers of the greater La Noscea region. While their descendants today are predominantly farmers, there are those who turned to shipping and fishery in those years when skirmishes with the kobolds stalled further exploration of the continent. Today, the Plainsfolk represent a significant part of the Lominsan populace, and are known for their relaxed, comfortable lifestyle.

options.label: Dunesfolk
options.description: The sons of fallen Mhach concealed themselves in the remote outlands for a time, before venturing into Thanalan in caravans propped on the backs of great beasts of burden. Living a nomadic existence in the sandy wastes, they came to be called by the name they bear today. It was the Dunesfolk who founded the great civilization of Belah'dia, which would later splinter into Sil'dih and Ul'dah, the latter of which prospers still today. Practical by nature and swift to put ideas into action, their temperament is well suited to seizing business opportunities, and it is little surprise that they played such a great role in building Ul'dah into the bustling center of trade and commerce it is today.

options.label: Seekers of the Sun
options.description: Unsurprisingly, given their self-bestowed clan name, the Seekers of the Sun count numerous devotees of Azeyma, the Warden, among their ranks. While their overall numbers are not great, their twenty-six tribes are scattered across all reaches of the realm, with small Seeker settlements to be found from the sands of the Sagolii Desert in southern Thanalan to the jagged peaks of Gyr Abania. Yet other Seekers have settled in Limsa Lominsa, drawn to the freedom of pirate life. Many Seekers, particularly those of the younger generation, choose to set off as adventurers, perhaps heeding the same call of the wild their ancestors once heard.

options.label: Keepers of the Moon
options.description: As might be surmised from their self-chosen name, the majority of the Keepers of the Moon are devout followers of Menphina. They reside and hunt freely in the Shroud, where for many years they came in conflict with the people of Gridania, who saw the Keepers as little more than poachers. In recent years, however, the two sides have reconciled their differences, and today many Keepers hunt in accordance with rules set by the Trappers' League, bartering the furs and meats they procure for agricultural goods and essential commodities. Others, however, refuse to bend to these rules, poaching the woods and laying waste to the natural environment as they see fit.

options.label: Sea Wolves
options.description: Descendants of a pirate clan long feared as the scourge of the Northern Empty, the Sea Wolves hail from the northern islands. Though many live there still today, a not-insignificant number left the northern islands seven centuries ago, eventually settling in Vylbrand. There, they established the maritime city-state of Limsa Lominsa, which prospered and took its place as one of Eorzea's great city-states. True to their seafaring roots, many Sea Wolves have made their mark as pirates, sailors, and fishermen. Most famous of them all is none other than Merlwyb Bloefhiswyn, Admiral of Limsa Lominsa.

options.label: Hellsguard
options.description: Few in number but burning with the fierce pride of warriors, the Hellsguard make their home in the desolate reaches of Abalathia's Spine. Their name is derived from the fiery peaks amidst which they founded their village—mountains of flame which they believe to be the gates to the underworld itself.

options.label: Raen
options.description: Believing themselves the children of the Dawn Father, the forebears of the Raen left behind their homeland to settle across Othard. They were received with hatred and hostility by other races in the early years, until a prominent warlord of Yanxia, impressed with their valor, forged an alliance with the strange race and took them on as retainers. Before long, the Raen had assumed a prominent role as warriors in the service of countless great warlords. Some ventured across the sea to the Far East, where they earned a reputation as legendary swordmasters.

options.label: Xaela
options.description: Children of the Dusk Mother of Auri creation, the Xaela have to this day not abandoned their ancestral home, living a nomadic life as hunters and gatherers on the vast Azim Steppe. With suitable grazing land sparse, conflict between individual tribes is common, with tribes forming, disbanding, and flying off in a ceaseless cycle of war and bloodshed. At last observation, Xaela tribes numbered fifty-one, though there is a high likelihood that recently splintered or merged tribes have rendered that count outdated.

options.label: Rava
options.description: Viera of the Rava clan live primarily in the Golmore Jungle, their umber skin allowing them to readily blend in with their surroundings. Though the males stand as wards of the forest, the females are adept hunters in their own right, fiercely guarding their homes and their young. Despite attempts by the Dalmascans to subjugate them, they have ever maintained a self-governing dominion. Though most would adhere to the traditions of the wood, some few have chosen to venture out into the world.

options.label: Veena
options.description: With skin as fair as the snowcapped mountains towering above, the Veena make their homes in the forests lining the southwestern foothills of the Skatay Range. Like the members of their sister clan, the Veena live as hunters and gatherers, laboring not only to protect the woods, but to nurture them. As the winds of war swept up a number of those who left their mountain homes, many such hardened hunters chose to set out for the distant shores of Eorzea.

options.label: Helions
options.description: Helions have traditionally been content to reside in southern Ilsabard with their respective tribes, devout servants to their queens, one and all—and thus have they only but recently begun to make their presence felt throughout the remainder of the three continents. Though these Hrothgar initially had no word to describe themselves, scholars came to call them "Helions" after observing how their lives all but revolved about their queen's needs, as planets circle the sun.

options.label: The Lost
options.description: Unlike their Helion brethren, the Lost are unbound by the whims of any reigning monarch, having long since found themselves bereft of the warm radiance of their queen. Most find that a nomadic lifestyle best suits their situation, and are known to ply a variety of trades that align with their propensity to travel—seasonal laborer, mercenary, and peddler among them.

options.label: Tank
options.description:
As a tank, your primary role is to shield the party from harm. Force your foes to focus their attention on you, thereby preventing them from endangering your friends and allies.
The most expedient way to do this is by charging headlong into the teeth of the enemy and using your abilities to inflict an enfeeblement called Enmity to discourage them from attacking your allies. Your stalwart presence on the battlefield also serves as a wall behind which your more fragile friends can shelter themselves from the storm of conflict. You, of course, need no such luxuries, as your high Defense and Max HP will keep you standing strong in the face of the fiercest tempest.
Your duty to protect your allies means you'll need to know when to play defensively and when to go on the attack. Some of your abilities can mitigate damage or grant enhancements, while others hit hard and deal a fair bit of damage. The support provided by your fellow adventurers will influence which you use and when, so be sure to coordinate your battle tactics with your party.

options.label: Healer
options.description:
As a healer, your primary role is to keep your allies hale and hearty by healing their wounds and removing enfeeblements.
Without you, your party has little hope of withstanding your enemies' attacks, so try to stay mobile and avoid taking damage whenever you can. You also need to keep tabs on your remaining MP; if you run out, you won't be able to offer aid to your allies. Be sure to think ahead and factor in your MP recovery when planning for future turns.

options.label: DPS
options.description: As a DPS, your primary role is to devastate your foes with potent attacks to secure victory for you and your fellow adventurers. DPS jobs are divided into three distinct types: melee DPS, physical ranged DPS, and magical ranged DPS.

options.label: Paladin
options.description:
As a paladin, you radiate an aura of unyielding righteousness that strikes fear in the hearts of the wicked.
When confronted with multiple foes, let loose with Total Eclipse or, after attaining level 50, Circle of Scorn to inflict Enmity en masse. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Paladin Combo and Rage of Halone. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Total Eclipse, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low.
Should you need to inflict Enmity on a foe in a pinch, Spirits Within or Provoke will do the trick. You don't always need to have Enmity on every enemy in an encounter, however. There's little point in spending an action to inflict Enmity on a foe if you expect them to fall during one of your allies' turns.
Once per round, you can use Sturdy Shield when an enemy attacks you with an ability to add 1 d6 to your Defense. With a little luck, you may even be able to negate a direct hit from a physical ability, so be sure to make use of this instant ability whenever you can.

options.label: Warrior
options.description:
Like a raging maelstrom sweeping the field of battle, warriors command the full attention of their opponents.
When confronted with multiple foes, charge into the fray and use Overpower to inflict Enmity on the lot of them. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage or an instant ability to replenish your HP.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Warrior Combo and Storm's Path. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Overpower, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low. Storm's Path dishes out damage while restoring HP—a surefire way to stay hale and hearty in the heat of battle while also helping hack down your foes.
With an arsenal that includes the Surging Tempest enhancement and the Berserk secondary ability, warriors are well equipped to dish out more damage than other tanks. You'll also have a lot of opportunities to accumulate Wrath as the encounter plays out, which can be spent to unleash powerful abilities that can really bring the pain. As the oft-repeated saying goes, the best defense is a good offense, so raise your axe high and lay your foes low.

options.label: Dark Knight
options.description:
Driven to seek justice at any cost, dark knights call upon the darkness within to vanquish those who would stand in their way.
When confronted with multiple foes, wade into the thick of battle and use Unleash to inflict Enmity on all around you. As affected enemies are likely to attack you, consider using Rampart or, after attaining level 40, Shadow Wall as your secondary action to reduce any incoming damage.
When engaging a smaller group of enemies, you can instead use your standard movement to get up close, then unleash Dark Knight Combo and Souleater. This strategy will allow you to deal more damage to a single target than is possible with Unleash, and you can always use your Combo trait to choose a different target for your second attack if your first strike brings your foe low. Souleater deals damage while restoring HP, allowing you to stay on your feet while cutting down your foes.
The Darkside enhancement lets you spend MP for a chance to boost your damage output. This can quickly drain your reserves, so make sure to use abilities that replenish MP whenever you need a top-up in order to get the most out of this unique enhancement.
Unlike other tanks, dark knights are capable of bringing both physical and magic abilities to bear against their foes. As the enemies you encounter are often more resilient against one of these at the expense of the other, learning to quickly recognize which type of ability is more effective in a given situation will undoubtedly prove a boon.

options.label: White Mage
options.description:
Wielders of the purifying art of white magic, white mages ensure their allies never falter in the face of adversity.
Though you may be tempted to use Cure II to restore a significant amount of HP to a wounded tank or other ally, keep in mind that any healing that exceeds the target's Max HP will go to waste. As a healer, your MP is a vital resource that can make the difference between victory and defeat in an encounter. If an ally hasn't suffered so much damage that they're in danger of being Knocked Out, consider conserving your MP by healing them with a simple Cure instead. After attaining level 40, the ability check for Cure has a chance to proc Freecure, which in turn reduces the cost of your next Cure II to 0 MP.
You can also inflict DOTs by using Aero, which becomes Aero II after attaining level 50. Granting allies Revivify with Regen—or Medica II after attaining level 50—can be a great way to be proactive with your healing, too. These effects last until the end of the phase, which means the earlier you get them up, the greater impact they'll have in the grand scheme of the encounter.
Learn to divide your attention between healing your allies and harrying your foes, and you'll ensure your party always emerges triumphant.

options.label: Scholar
options.description:
As a scholar, your tactical prowess enables you to guide your allies to victory on the field of battle, all the while mending their wounds in tandem with your summoned faerie.
Your pet, the faerie Eos, takes her turn immediately before you, so you'll constantly need to consider where to position her and which of her abilities to have her use. So long as you haven't used Dissipation—which you gain access to after attaining level 60—Eos will aid you in healing your allies for the entirety of an encounter.
Of course, your own abilities do more than simply restore HP—scholars specialize in erecting barriers that prevent their allies from taking damage in the first place, as well as using secondary and instant abilities to chip away at their enemies' HP. Keep in mind that a character cannot have more than one barrier at a time, and when a new barrier is granted, the one with the lower HP value is lost. A wise tactician always keeps a cool head so that they may judge when their barriers are needed and plan accordingly.
After attaining level 50, you gain access to Sacred Soil, an ability that creates an area in which allies suffer reduced damage. This area cannot be moved once deployed, so make use of your tactical ingenuity and select the most favorable position on the encounter map.

options.label: Astrologian
options.description:
As an astrologian, you possess the wisdom to influence the fate of your fellow adventurers by interpreting the patterns of the stars in the heavens.
While you are well equipped to keep your allies fighting fit by restoring HP and granting Revivify, you can also support your party by empowering a single ally with Major Arcana at the start of your turn with your Play Arcana trait. Major Arcana allows this ally to reroll a single die when determining the damage dealt by an ability, which improves their chances of inflicting a significant blow to your opposition. Don't forget to make use of your Play Arcana trait at the start of each of your turns to harness your full potential.
You also have several instant abilities that affect all allies within an area around you. Try to position yourself within range of your party members while staying out of your enemies' reach so you can heal up your comrades at a moment's notice and divine the path to victory.

options.label: Combo
options.description: After resolving the effects of an ability with Combo, you may use one of the specified abilities at any point during your turn. You may move before doing so, and may choose a new target when using this additional ability.

options.label: Oath Mastery
options.description: Certain effects grant you Conviction. You can have up to 4 Conviction at any given time. At the start of your turn, gain 1 Conviction.

options.label: Enhanced Enmity
options.description: Enemies that you have Enmity on incur a -8 penalty on all ability checks that do not target you.
